title: Raster
description: A song title set in letters drawn only from horizontal and vertical strokes with 45-degree corners on a 5 x 9 design grid, and rendered only by a dot raster: each cell measures how much of its area the letters cover, at 8 x 8 samples, and prints one dot of that size, from a pinpoint to a full square. Drag up or down and the pitch slides continuously from five cells across a letter to twenty. Where it divides the design grid the letters lock clean, with half-tone dots on every cut; between, stems and cuts land on every phase of the screen and beat bands travel through the word as you drag. Type to change the title.
intent: After Wim Crouwel's New Alphabet (1967), https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/New_Alphabet, and his Vormgevers poster grid: accept the raster completely and let the letterforms come from it. Own glyphs, not the font.
